Clean a binary root image

Source: R/clean_image.R
clean_image.Rd

Performs three sequential cleaning operations on a binary segmented image:

  1. Hole filling – fills black regions enclosed by white (segmentation gaps inside roots).

  2. Speck removal – deletes isolated foreground blobs not connected to the image border (false-positive root detections).

  3. Edge smoothing (optional, off by default) – applies morphological closing to smooth jagged root edges.

Usage

clean_image(
  img,
  fill_holes_upto = NULL,
  drop_objects_upto = NULL,
  size_unit = c("px", "mm2"),
  dpi = NULL,
  protect_border = FALSE,
  edge_smooth = FALSE,
  kernel_shape = "disk",
  kernel_size = 3,
  iterations = 1,
  select_layer = NULL,
  output_format = "spatrast",
  report = FALSE,
  max_hole_size = NULL,
  max_artifact_size = NULL
)

Arguments

img

A cimg object, SpatRaster, matrix, or file path (binary mask).

fill_holes_upto

Largest enclosed hole that gets filled; anything bigger is left alone. NULL (default) fills every enclosed hole. Units are set by size_unit. See Choosing thresholds above.

drop_objects_upto

Largest disconnected foreground blob that gets deleted; anything bigger is kept. NULL (default) deletes every candidate blob. Units are set by size_unit.

size_unit

Unit of the two thresholds above: "px" (default, pixel count) or "mm2" (square millimetres, which requires dpi).

dpi

Scan resolution, required when size_unit = "mm2" and ignored otherwise.

protect_border

Logical. If TRUE, white regions touching the image border are kept regardless of size (roots leaving the frame). If FALSE (default), border-touching specks are removed by the same drop_objects_upto test as anything else – being at the edge does not protect an artifact.

edge_smooth

Logical. Apply morphological closing after hole/artifact cleaning. Default FALSE.

kernel_shape

Structuring element shape for edge smoothing: "disk" (default), "square", or "diamond".

kernel_size

Structuring element size (odd integer). Default 3.

iterations

Number of closing iterations for edge smoothing. Default 1.

select_layer

Integer or NULL. Which layer to use for multi-layer inputs.

output_format

Character. Format of the returned object. One of "spatrast" (default), "cimg", or "matrix". Using "spatrast" means the result can be passed directly to terra::plot(), skeletonize_image(), root_length(), etc. without any further conversion.

report

Logical. If TRUE, also calls report_image_components on the original (uncleaned) image before cleaning. When output_format = "spatrast" (default), the cleaned raster is returned directly even when report = TRUE; the report is printed as a side effect. Default FALSE.

max_hole_size, max_artifact_size

Deprecated names for fill_holes_upto and drop_objects_upto. Supplying either warns and sets the corresponding new argument.

Value

A cleaned image in the format specified by output_format (SpatRaster, cimg, or matrix).

Why clean before skeletonization

skeletonize_image() uses the Medial Axis Transform, which is driven by the distance transform. Small holes inside a root inflate the local distance values and force the medial axis to bifurcate around the hole, producing spurious branching points. Isolated artifact pixels produce phantom skeleton segments. Cleaning first yields a much cleaner skeleton.

Choosing thresholds

Call report_image_components on your image first to see the actual pixel counts of all holes and specks. At 300 dpi, sensible starting values are fill_holes_upto = 50 and drop_objects_upto = 10 pixels.

A pixel threshold means a different physical size at every scan resolution: 50 px is 0.36 mm\(^2\) at 300 dpi but 0.022 mm\(^2\) at 1200 dpi, so a call tuned on one dataset cleans differently on another. Set size_unit = "mm2" and supply dpi to give the thresholds a fixed physical meaning that carries across resolutions.

Edge smoothing caution

edge_smooth = TRUE applies a morphological closing that slightly dilates then erodes root edges. This can merge closely adjacent roots and alter root diameter measurements. Only use it when the segmentation output has very jagged edges; leave it off (FALSE, the default) otherwise.

Input must be binary

clean_image() operates on a binary mask (root = 1, background = 0). If your input is a raw probability / grayscale image from a segmentation model, binarize it first with image_threshold and pass the result here.

See also

report_image_components, skeletonize_image, image_threshold

Examples

data(seg_Oulanka2023_Session01_T067)
img <- terra::rast(seg_Oulanka2023_Session01_T067)


# Clean: fill small holes, delete tiny specks -- returns SpatRaster
cleaned <- clean_image(img,
                       fill_holes_upto   = 50,
                       drop_objects_upto = 10,
                       select_layer      = 2)

# The same thresholds expressed physically, so they mean the same thing
# whatever the scan resolution
cleaned_mm <- clean_image(img,
                          fill_holes_upto   = 0.36,
                          drop_objects_upto = 0.07,
                          size_unit         = "mm2",
                          dpi               = 300,
                          select_layer      = 2)

# If you need a cimg for further imager operations:
cleaned_cimg <- clean_image(img, fill_holes_upto = 50,
                            output_format = "cimg", select_layer = 2)
